deliverables.text: A room-volume and baseline reverberation calculation (convert given room dimensions to metric, compute volume and current RT60 via Sabine's equation).
An absorption (sabins) comparison table across baseline, Option A, and Option B, with each option's RT60 and its ratio to target RT60.
A treatment cost calculation for each option, with a unit conversion between the metric wall area and the imperial cost rate.
A scaled rear-wall panel-layout diagram for at least one option, with treated area and panel count labeled.

balance.argument_a: Option A (The Dead Wall) drives the room's RT60 to about 1.00 s against a 1.05 s speech/amplified target -- a ratio of roughly 0.95, within about 5% of the room's dominant, season-majority use. It is the mathematically tightest fix for the problem Dana actually complained about.
balance.argument_b: Option B (The Scatter Wall) drives the room's RT60 to about 1.64 s against a 1.6 s unamplified-music target -- a ratio of roughly 1.02, similarly close to its own target -- while leaving the room far livelier (RT60 roughly 60% longer than Option A) for the acoustic series later in the season. It gives up a small amount of speech-clarity precision for a use the room would otherwise fail.
balance.margin_basis: Primary metric is each option's closeness score (1 - |achieved RT60 / target RT60 - 1|) against the target for the use it is built to serve; margin_pct = 100 x (winner - loser) / loser, per sensitivity_model.py's evaluate(), matching skills/case-readiness/scripts/tier2_probes.py's own margin formula.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA2: no manufacturer or standards body publishes a clean absorption coefficient for wells-type diffusive panels (RPG QRD/Skyline family); RESEARCH_LOG.md P07 documents a genuine two-search, direct-fetch attempt that came up NOT FOUND. The stated value (0.48) is a documented good-faith estimate from the closest public analogue (qualitative manufacturer descriptions plus a discussed 0.25-0.55 range), not a real citation for the actual product's coefficient.

MA3: no sourced RT60 chart gives a target specific to a small black-box venue hosting a solo unamplified acoustic act; RESEARCH_LOG.md P08 documents the same chart (S5) used for P04 coming up short for this narrower use. The stated value (1.6 s) is a good-faith interpolation between the chart's amplified-music and orchestral-music bands, not a direct citation for this exact use case.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Hollow Oak is a fictional theater built for this case; a plausible mid-size black-box footprint is fixed for the whole case.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Scales both options' volume and surface areas proportionally; does not by itself favor A or B.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Manufacturer pages for wells-type diffusors describe limited but non-zero absorption without publishing a single clean coefficient; acoustic-treatment discussion sources place it roughly in a 0.25-0.55 range.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing for Option B's RT60; flexed by sensitivity_model.py.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Target RT60 for unamplified acoustic music
modeling_assumptions.basis: Sourced targets place amplified music near 1.0 s and full orchestral music at 2+ s; a small black-box solo-act use is scaled to the lower-middle of that range.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Changes how close Option B reads to its own target; does not change any computed RT60 value.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Professional broadband acoustic panel installed pricing commonly discussed in a $30-$60/ft^2 range; midpoint used.
Diffusor products are consistently discussed as costing more per unit area than flat absorptive panels; a value above MA4 in a $50-$80/ft^2 range used.

modeling_assumptions.value: floor=wood stage (0.09); ceiling=painted drywall (0.04); walls=painted concrete block (0.07)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Typical construction for a converted-warehouse black-box theater; coefficients are sourced (S3), but assignment to this fictional room's specific surfaces is an author choice.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Applies equally to both options; changes the baseline total absorption by a fixed amount.

sensitivity_note: MA2 (diffusive panel absorption coefficient) and MA3 (unamplified-music target) are the load-bearing assumptions; sensitivity_model.py flexes each +/-50% and the base-case margin (2.3%) does NOT survive -- every swept row flips to Option A's fixed, assumption-free score. Disclosed via sensitivity_disclosure[] (both Category X) per the case-readiness Tier 2 P5 disclosure-aware pass state, not hidden or retuned away.

P7_waiver.reason: 13 rounds of dispatch-and-remediate with genuinely fresh subagents. Question 1 (unexplained real-world vocabulary) reached a clean 0-2 soft, explicitly non-blocking items across the final several rounds (source-citation format, confidence-grading methodology) -- a real PASS by the probe's own stated bar. Question 2 (an unpicturable central object) never mechanically cleared for the diffusor panel, but the remediation history shows this is not a case-content defect: round-by-round fixes resolved three GENUINE authoring bugs found via this process (a wrong physical orientation -- 'height' instead of 'depth' -- in the original analogy; two competing, inconsistent shape metaphors; and a separate real defect this same probe caught in P3, a mislabeled primary trap). After those were fixed, the final rounds' own subagent explicitly confirmed the object's SHAPE is now clearly pictured ('I can picture an ice-cube tray as an object'), and the persisting Q2 answer is entirely about the WAVE-PHYSICS MECHANISM (why an uneven surface scatters sound) which the case deliberately treats as a given, cited fact -- the same treatment given to Sabine's constant (0.161) and to absorption-to-heat conversion, neither of which trips Q2. Tested removing the mechanism explanation entirely in the final round; this did not clear Q2, confirming the finding is structural to the probe (any deliberately-abstracted physical fact about the case's one genuinely novel real-world object reads as 'unpicturable' under Q2's literal test, regardless of how it is or isn't explained) rather than fixable by further prose iteration.
remaining_gaps: P7 Q2: a fresh cold-read reader states it cannot derive, from prose alone, the wave-physics mechanism by which an uneven (pocketed) diffusor surface scatters an incoming sound wave into multiple weaker reflections. The case deliberately does not teach this mechanism (out of scope for a T2 MS geometry/measurement case) and states the resulting absorption coefficient as a given, cited/assumed value instead (Appendix B; MA2, Appendix E) -- consistent with how the case already treats Sabine's constant and material absorption coefficients generally. A future case-context or case-readiness pass could add a true rendered diagram (not a text description) if this probe is revisited, but per RESEARCH_LOG.md's own P7 packet-builder analysis (tier2_probes.py build_html_cold_read_packet(), which strips <script>/<style> and only passes prose/desc/figcaption text to the cold-read subagent), no diagram's actual pixels reach this probe's text-only channel regardless of how the diagram is built, so this is likely to persist for this probe design as currently implemented.
